claim: Electron cryo-microscopy (cryo-EM) has been used as a method to visualize biological macromolecules in their native-hydrated state for more than three decades.
source: Electron cryo-microscopy (cryo-EM) has been used as a method to visualize biological macromolecules in their native-hydrated state for more than three decades (Adrian et al., 1984).
evidence: Supported by citation to Adrian et al., 1984

claim: Major improvements in detector technology and associated computational procedures recently transformed single-particle cryo-EM.
source: Major improvements in detector technology (Faruqi and Henderson, 2007; McMullan et al., 2016) and associated computational procedures recently transformed single-particle cryo-EM that since has been producing a plenitude of near-atomic resolution structures from specimens of lower symmetry (Allegretti et al., 2014; Amunts et al., 2014; Bai et al., 2013) and lower molecular weight than previously deemed possible (Bai et al., 2015; Liao et al., 2013; Merk et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to detector technology improvements and resulting structural achievements

claim: Single-particle cryo-EM has been producing near-atomic resolution structures from specimens of lower symmetry and lower molecular weight than previously deemed possible.
source: Major improvements in detector technology (Faruqi and Henderson, 2007; McMullan et al., 2016) and associated computational procedures recently transformed single-particle cryo-EM that since has been producing a plenitude of near-atomic resolution structures from specimens of lower symmetry (Allegretti et al., 2014; Amunts et al., 2014; Bai et al., 2013) and lower molecular weight than previously deemed possible (Bai et al., 2015; Liao et al., 2013; Merk et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple recent structural studies

claim: At near-atomic resolution, reconstructed EM density maps contain sufficient detail to interpret the structure using atomic models.
source: At this resolution, the reconstructed EM density maps contain sufficient detail to interpret the structure using atomic models.
evidence: Based on established understanding of resolution requirements for atomic modeling

claim: The building and refinement of atomic models present a critical step in the structure determination process.
source: The building and refinement of atomic models thus present a critical step in the structure determination process and their accuracy depends on the quality of the EM density.
evidence: Based on established understanding of structural biology workflows

claim: The accuracy of atomic models depends on the quality of the EM density.
source: The building and refinement of atomic models thus present a critical step in the structure determination process and their accuracy depends on the quality of the EM density.
evidence: Based on logical relationship between data quality and model accuracy

claim: Coordinate refinement in X-ray crystallography typically depends on initial phase estimates that are iteratively improved.
source: Coordinate refinement in X-ray crystallography typically depends on initial phase estimates that are iteratively improved (Agarwal and Isaacs, 1977; Grosse-Kunstleve et al., 2002; Lunin et al., 2002; Read, 1986; Wilson, 1942).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to crystallographic refinement methods

claim: Crystallographic refinement successively improves map interpretability throughout the refinement procedure.
source: As a result, crystallographic refinement successively improves map interpretability throughout the refinement procedure.
evidence: Inferred from the iterative improvement of phase estimates in crystallography

claim: The cryo-EM experiment yields both amplitudes and phases directly from images.
source: By contrast, the cryo-EM experiment yields both amplitudes and phases directly from images and experimentally determined EM density can therefore be used as a constant minimization target (Grigorieff et al., 1996; Unwin, 2005; Yonekura et al., 2003).
evidence: Supported by citations and established knowledge of cryo-EM methodology

claim: Experimentally determined EM density can be used as a constant minimization target.
source: By contrast, the cryo-EM experiment yields both amplitudes and phases directly from images and experimentally determined EM density can therefore be used as a constant minimization target (Grigorieff et al., 1996; Unwin, 2005; Yonekura et al., 2003).
evidence: Supported by citations to cryo-EM refinement methods

claim: The commonly accepted procedure for resolution estimation in cryo-EM is the Fourier shell correlation (FSC).
source: The commonly accepted procedure for resolution estimation in cryo-EM is the Fourier shell correlation (FSC), which measures the correlation of Fourier coefficients in resolution shells between independent map reconstructions (Harauz and van Heel, 1986; Saxton and Baumeister, 1982; van Heel et al., 1982).
evidence: Supported by citations to FSC methodology papers

claim: FSC measures the correlation of Fourier coefficients in resolution shells between independent map reconstructions.
source: The commonly accepted procedure for resolution estimation in cryo-EM is the Fourier shell correlation (FSC), which measures the correlation of Fourier coefficients in resolution shells between independent map reconstructions (Harauz and van Heel, 1986; Saxton and Baumeister, 1982; van Heel et al., 1982).
evidence: Supported by citations defining FSC methodology

claim: The reported map resolution corresponds to a pre-defined cut-off of the FSC curve.
source: The reported map resolution corresponds to a pre-defined cut-off of the FSC curve (Rosenthal and Henderson, 2003).
evidence: Supported by citation to Rosenthal and Henderson 2003

claim: It is common practice to low-pass filter cryo-EM volumes at the resolution cut-off.
source: Currently, it is common practice to low-pass filter cryo-EM volumes at this resolution cut-off.
evidence: Based on established practice in the cryo-EM field

claim: Many recently determined EM density maps contain regions that differ substantially from the overall resolution due to varying flexibility and/or subunit occupancy.
source: Many of the recently determined EM density maps, however, contain regions that differ substantially from this overall resolution due to varying flexibility and/or subunit occupancy in different parts of the structure (Bai et al., 2013; Hoffmann et al., 2015; Zhao et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to studies demonstrating local resolution variation

claim: The quality of the reconstruction is poorer at the particle periphery when compared with the particle center due to limitations of current 3D reconstruction algorithms.
source: In addition to inherent flexibility of macromolecular complexes, the quality of the reconstruction is poorer at the particle periphery when compared with the particle center due to limitations of current three-dimensional (3D) reconstruction algorithms.
evidence: Based on known limitations of 3D reconstruction methods

claim: The average FSC measurement falls short of describing local resolution differences in different parts of the structure.
source: In providing an estimate of overall map resolution, the average FSC measurement falls short of describing such local resolution differences in different parts of the structure (Cardone et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to Cardone et al. 2013 on local resolution

claim: Density contrast is critical for map interpretation.
source: In addition to resolution, density contrast is critical for map interpretation.
evidence: Based on established understanding of map interpretation requirements

claim: High-resolution contrast in cryo-EM maps is attenuated by a resolution-dependent amplitude falloff.
source: High-resolution contrast in cryo-EM maps is attenuated by a resolution-dependent amplitude falloff.
evidence: Based on known physical properties of cryo-EM imaging

claim: Sharpening with a uniform map B-factor partially restores contrast loss in cryo-EM maps.
source: Compensation is achieved by sharpening with a uniform map B-factor, which partially restores contrast loss in cryo-EM maps (Rosenthal and Henderson, 2003) and in low-resolution electron density maps from X-ray crystallography (DeLaBarre and Brunger, 2003; Jacobson et al., 1961; Stehle and Harrison, 1996).
evidence: Supported by citations to B-factor sharpening methods

claim: A signal-to-noise weighting scheme based on the FSC equivalent to the crystallographic figure-of-merit (FOM) is commonly used to avoid noise amplification at high resolution.
source: To avoid noise amplification at high resolution, a signal-to-noise weighting scheme based on the FSC equivalent to the crystallographic figure-of-merit (FOM) is commonly used (Rosenthal and Henderson, 2003).
evidence: Supported by citation to Rosenthal and Henderson 2003

claim: The B-factor can be estimated numerically.
source: The B-factor can be estimated numerically (DeLaBarre and Brunger, 2003; Rosenthal and Henderson, 2003), but in practice often needs to be fine-tuned empirically in an effort to generate optimal contrast.
evidence: Supported by citations to B-factor estimation methods

claim: In practice, the B-factor often needs to be fine-tuned empirically to generate optimal contrast.
source: The B-factor can be estimated numerically (DeLaBarre and Brunger, 2003; Rosenthal and Henderson, 2003), but in practice often needs to be fine-tuned empirically in an effort to generate optimal contrast.
evidence: Based on practical experience in the field

claim: Alternative scaling procedures use the X-ray solution scattering (SAXS) curve of the specimen to correct the amplitudes.
source: Alternative scaling procedures use the X-ray solution scattering (SAXS) curve of the specimen (Gabashvili et al., 2000; Schmid et al., 1999) or the radially averaged amplitude profile of the crystal structure (Falke et al., 2005) to correct the amplitudes accordingly.
evidence: Supported by citations to SAXS-based scaling methods

claim: Alternative scaling procedures use the radially averaged amplitude profile of the crystal structure to correct the amplitudes.
source: Alternative scaling procedures use the X-ray solution scattering (SAXS) curve of the specimen (Gabashvili et al., 2000; Schmid et al., 1999) or the radially averaged amplitude profile of the crystal structure (Falke et al., 2005) to correct the amplitudes accordingly.
evidence: Supported by citation to Falke et al. 2005

claim: Building and refinement of atomic models have become the ultimate steps of cryo-EM structure determination with recent near-atomic resolution cryo-EM reconstructions.
source: With the wealth of recent near-atomic resolution cryo-EM reconstructions (Cheng, 2015; KühlbrandtKuhlbrandt, 2014; Subramaniam et al., 2016), building and refinement of atomic models have become the ultimate steps of cryo-EM structure determination.
evidence: Supported by citations to reviews of recent cryo-EM achievements

claim: New approaches are required to optimize the process of sharpening by objective means and to better integrate model refinement with map interpretation.
source: Therefore, new approaches are required to optimize the process of sharpening by objective means and to better integrate model refinement with map interpretation.
evidence: This is a statement of need based on the limitations described in the introduction

claim: Crystallographic model refinement routinely uses prior information from atomic models to enhance the clarity of electron density maps.
source: Crystallographic model refinement routinely uses prior information from atomic models to enhance the clarity of electron density maps.
evidence: Based on established crystallographic refinement practices

claim: As the crystallographic model improves, better phase estimates iteratively make the electron density more interpretable.
source: As the model improves, better phase estimates iteratively make the electron density more interpretable and ultimately provide more accurate structures.
evidence: Based on established understanding of crystallographic refinement

claim: Current cryo-EM density interpretation does not make use of model information.
source: Current cryo-EM density interpretation does not make use of model information and model refinement strategies leave the target density unchanged.
evidence: Based on description of current cryo-EM practices

claim: Current cryo-EM model refinement strategies leave the target density unchanged.
source: Current cryo-EM density interpretation does not make use of model information and model refinement strategies leave the target density unchanged.
evidence: Based on description of current cryo-EM practices

claim: The authors present a general procedure that utilizes prior model information to iteratively compute map representations better suited for interpretation and atomic model refinement.
source: We here present a general procedure that utilizes prior model information to iteratively compute map representations better suited for interpretation and atomic model refinement than those obtained from existing approaches.
evidence: This is the main claim of the paper describing the new method

claim: The LocScale procedure optimizes map contrast by local amplitude scaling against an atomic structure.
source: The procedure optimizes map contrast by local amplitude scaling against an atomic structure and thereby implicitly accounts for differences in local resolution.
evidence: This describes the mechanism of the LocScale method

claim: The LocScale procedure implicitly accounts for differences in local resolution.
source: The procedure optimizes map contrast by local amplitude scaling against an atomic structure and thereby implicitly accounts for differences in local resolution.
evidence: This describes a property of the LocScale method

claim: Model-based local sharpening can increase interpretability of density maps in particular in cases of resolution variation.
source: By testing the procedure using six cryo-EM structures of TRPV1, β-galactosidase, γ-secretase, ribosome-EF-Tu complex, 20S proteasome and RNA polymerase III, we illustrate how local sharpening can increase interpretability of density maps in particular in cases of resolution variation and facilitates model building and atomic model refinement.
evidence: Supported by testing on six different cryo-EM structures

claim: Model-based local sharpening facilitates model building and atomic model refinement.
source: By testing the procedure using six cryo-EM structures of TRPV1, β-galactosidase, γ-secretase, ribosome-EF-Tu complex, 20S proteasome and RNA polymerase III, we illustrate how local sharpening can increase interpretability of density maps in particular in cases of resolution variation and facilitates model building and atomic model refinement.
evidence: Supported by testing on six different cryo-EM structures

claim: The appearance of map features depends on the relative magnitude of frequency components, not only on the presence of amplitude and phase signal.
source: The appearance of map features does not only depend on the presence of amplitude and phase signal at the corresponding resolution, but also on the relative magnitude of these frequency components.
evidence: Based on Fourier theory and demonstrated with test images

claim: Cryo-EM images are affected by amplitude modulations due to the contrast-transfer function.
source: This is particularly true for cryo-EM images that are affected by amplitude modulations due to the contrast-transfer function (Erickson and Klug, 1970).
evidence: Supported by citation to Erickson and Klug 1970

claim: Substituting image amplitudes with random Gaussian noise while keeping phases results in poor contrast and difficult feature discrimination.
source: For illustration purposes, we substituted the amplitudes of the image with random Gaussian noise and computed the inverse Fourier transform of the hybrid image. Although this image still has perfect phases and the overall image information is largely conserved, it shows poor contrast and thus makes feature discrimination difficult, and in part impossible (Figure 1B).
evidence: Demonstrated with test image manipulation shown in Figure 1B

claim: Image amplitudes of the test image decay exponentially towards higher frequencies.
source: As reflected in the radial amplitude profile of the original image, image amplitudes decay exponentially towards higher frequencies.
evidence: Shown in Figure 1A radial amplitude profile

claim: Amplitudes of cryo-EM maps decay much faster than photographic images due to imaging imperfections.
source: Amplitudes of cryo-EM maps decay much faster due to imaging imperfections (Henderson, 1992).
evidence: Supported by citation to Henderson 1992

claim: Scaling amplitudes by an approximated exponential falloff restores the overall magnitude distribution and improves image contrast.
source: Scaling amplitudes by an approximated exponential falloff restores the overall magnitude distribution at low and high frequencies and improves image contrast (Figure 1C).
evidence: Demonstrated with test image shown in Figure 1C

claim: Scaling amplitudes by an approximated exponential falloff is equivalent to the widely used cryo-EM map sharpening procedure with a numerically estimated B-factor.
source: This procedure is equivalent to the widely used cryo-EM map sharpening procedure with a numerically estimated B-factor.
evidence: Based on established understanding of B-factor sharpening

claim: Better contrast can be obtained by scaling amplitudes against the radial average of the original image.
source: Better contrast can be obtained by more accurately restoring amplitude differences between adjacent frequency components. This can be achieved by scaling amplitudes against the radial average of the original image, equivalent to so-called reference-based scaling of cryo-EM maps using an X-ray model or solution scattering profile (Figure 1D).
evidence: Demonstrated with test image shown in Figure 1D

claim: Local image scaling yields more accurate amplitude distributions than global amplitude correction.
source: Moreover, as the radially averaged amplitude profile sums many features across the image, the relative distribution of adjacent frequency components may not be optimally restored by global amplitude correction. We therefore tested whether local image scaling can yield more accurate amplitude distributions.
evidence: This is a hypothesis tested with the tile-based scaling procedure

claim: Tile-based local amplitude scaling better restores high-resolution contrast including directional amplitude components compared to global scaling.
source: In this image, high-resolution contrast including directional amplitude components is better restored when compared with that scaled against the global average, and the power spectrum more closely resembles that of the original image (Figure 1E).
evidence: Demonstrated with test image shown in Figure 1E

claim: Contrast restoration by tile-based amplitude scaling against a local reference should be preferred over compensating amplitude decay by an exponential or overall falloff approximation.
source: This 2D example highlights the importance of relative amplitude scaling for local image contrast and shows that contrast restoration by tile-based amplitude scaling against a local reference should be preferred over compensating amplitude decay by an exponential or an overall falloff approximation.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from the 2D test image experiments

claim: Cryo-EM maps display local resolution variations in addition to steep amplitude decay towards high resolution.
source: Due to the contrast benefit of reference-based local amplitude scaling in photographic images, we set out to assess whether this strategy also improves contrast restoration in cryo-EM density maps. Contrary to the 2D image with uniform resolution, cryo-EM maps display local resolution variations in addition to the steep amplitude decay towards high resolution (Figure 1F).
evidence: Shown in Figure 1F with local FSC calculation for TRPV1

claim: Locally determined B-factors vary across deposited 3D cryo-EM densities.
source: We quantified this amplitude decay and mapped locally determined B-factors to four deposited 3D densities from the EM databank (Figure 1G, Figure 1–figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: Shown in Figure 1G and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A-C for multiple structures

claim: Estimating B-factors by linear fitting to Guinier profiles is error-prone with coefficients of determination R2 ranging from 0.6 to 0.9.
source: It should be noted that estimating B-factors by linear fitting to Guinier profiles is error-prone with coefficients of determination R2 ranging from 0.6 to 0.9, in particular in areas of poorer resolution (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A,D and E).
evidence: Shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A,D,E

claim: Locally adjusted sharpening levels may be required to optimally represent density features in maps with significant local resolution variation.
source: The results from our four test cases suggest that locally adjusted sharpening levels may be required to optimally represent density features, in particular for maps with significant local resolution variation.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from analysis of four test cases

claim: The LocScale procedure adapts the relative amplitude levels required to optimize local contrast by imposing the expected radially averaged amplitude profile.
source: Within a rolling density window, this procedure adapts the relative amplitude levels required to optimize local contrast by imposing the expected radially averaged amplitude profile for the structure contained within it, and by acting as a convoluted Gaussian low-pass filter that reduces background noise (Figure 2B).
evidence: Description of the LocScale mechanism illustrated in Figure 2B

claim: The LocScale procedure acts as a convoluted Gaussian low-pass filter that reduces background noise.
source: Within a rolling density window, this procedure adapts the relative amplitude levels required to optimize local contrast by imposing the expected radially averaged amplitude profile for the structure contained within it, and by acting as a convoluted Gaussian low-pass filter that reduces background noise (Figure 2B).
evidence: Description of the LocScale mechanism illustrated in Figure 2B

claim: All sharpening techniques considerably enhance interpretability of the density beyond the unsharpened EMD-5778.
source: All techniques, including global B-factor sharpening, considerably enhance interpretability of the density beyond that of EMD-5778 (Figure 2C).
evidence: Shown in Figure 2C comparing different sharpening methods

claim: UNSHARP and LocScale maps contain lower levels of peripheral noise compared with maps obtained by sharpening using locally estimated Guinier B-factors.
source: The comparison of the results obtained with the three local sharpening procedures reveals that UNSHARP and LocScale maps contain lower levels of peripheral noise compared with maps obtained by sharpening using locally estimated Guinier B-factors despite the FOM weighting.
evidence: Shown in Figure 2C comparing different sharpening methods

claim: Global sharpening can lead to overrepresentation of high frequency components.
source: Comparison of the profiles further suggests that global sharpening can lead to overrepresentation of high frequency components, whereas the LocScale map displays the expected smooth falloff towards high frequencies.
evidence: Shown in Figure 2D comparing radial amplitude profiles

claim: The LocScale map displays the expected smooth falloff towards high frequencies.
source: Comparison of the profiles further suggests that global sharpening can lead to overrepresentation of high frequency components, whereas the LocScale map displays the expected smooth falloff towards high frequencies.
evidence: Shown in Figure 2D comparing radial amplitude profiles

claim: UNSHARP masking results in attenuation of low frequencies.
source: This behavior arises from the local distribution of atomic B-factors that determines the steepness of the amplitude falloff and thus implicitly also accounts for local resolution differences (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D–H). Unlike the other sharpening methods, UNSHARP masking appears to result in attenuation of low frequencies (Figure 2D).
evidence: Shown in Figure 2D comparing radial amplitude profiles

claim: All sharpening approaches can be adjusted locally to reveal a high level of interpretable detail in well-defined map regions.
source: Inspection of well-defined map regions (e.g. residues 430–449) indicates that all sharpening approaches can be adjusted locally such that they reveal a high level of interpretable detail (Figure 2E).
evidence: Shown in Figure 2E for TRPV1 residues 430-449

claim: Numerical B-factor based approaches show poorer quality density in peripheral map regions resolved at lower than average resolution.
source: Numerical B-factor based approaches, however, show poorer quality density in particular in peripheral map regions resolved at lower than average resolution.
evidence: Shown in Figure 2F comparing peripheral regions

claim: Density from UNSHARP masking appears more blurred in less well-resolved regions when compared with the LocScale map.
source: While reproducing density comparably sharp in well-resolved regions, density from UNSHARP masking appears more blurred in less well-resolved regions when compared with the LocScale map (Figure 2F).
evidence: Shown in Figure 2F comparing peripheral regions

claim: Reference-based sharpening by local amplitude scaling provides a robust way to appropriately sharpen and filter all regions in a map simultaneously.
source: In conclusion, reference-based sharpening by local amplitude scaling provides a robust way to appropriately sharpen and filter all regions in a map simultaneously such that they conform to the expected amplitude falloff.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from comparison of sharpening methods

claim: Features in the deposited Pol III map are sharpening artifacts inconsistent with molecular structure.
source: At first sight, the Pol III LocScale map appears less featured at the peripheral subunits when compared with EMD-3180. However, closer inspection reveals that features in the deposited map in fact are sharpening artifacts inconsistent with molecular structure (Figure 3A, upper panel).
evidence: Shown in Figure 3A upper panel

claim: LocScale sharpening eliminates artifacts resulting from incorrect amplitude scaling.
source: By contrast, LocScale sharpening eliminates such artifacts resulting from incorrect amplitude scaling (Figure 3A, lower panel).
evidence: Shown in Figure 3A lower panel

claim: The LocScale map of TRPV1 reveals more clearly resolved α-helical pitch and well-defined side chain densities compared to the deposited EMD-5778 map.
source: This comparison reveals more clearly resolved α-helical pitch and well-defined side chain densities in the LocScale map (Figure 3B, lower panel), which are not as readily discernible in the uniformly sharpened and filtered deposited map (Figure 3B, upper panel).
evidence: Shown in Figure 3B comparing TRPV1 maps

claim: Optimized contrast improves visibility of high-resolution features from map regions at higher than average resolution in addition to dampening noise in regions at lower than average resolution.
source: In effect, the optimized contrast improves visibility of high-resolution features from map regions at higher than average resolution in addition to dampening noise in regions at lower than average resolution.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from comparison of LocScale with other methods

claim: Local sharpening helps increase interpretability of cryo-EM density maps by optimally restoring local map contrast.
source: Local sharpening helps increase interpretability of cryo-EM density maps by optimally restoring local map contrast.
evidence: Summary conclusion from the results

claim: No phase information is transferred from the model to the scaled density maps throughout the LocScale procedure.
source: We note here that throughout the LocScale procedure no phase information is transferred from the model to the scaled density maps.
evidence: Description of the LocScale method properties

claim: Information from model amplitudes radially averaged over a finite-sized density window is used to correct the power of Fourier amplitudes in the experimental frequency spectrum.
source: However, information from model amplitudes radially averaged over a finite-sized density window is used to correct the power of Fourier amplitudes in the experimental frequency spectrum.
evidence: Description of the LocScale method mechanism

claim: Side chain density for F436 is clearly visible in the scaled map despite the absence of side chain density in the F436A mutant reference map.
source: In a first experiment, we substituted F436 to alanine and used the F436A mutant to compute a reference map. Despite the absence of side chain density in the reference map, side chain density for F436 is clearly visible in the scaled map.
evidence: Shown in Figure 3C-D with F436A mutant reference

claim: No additional density is visible in the scaled map for V440W despite W440 density being present in the reference map.
source: In a second experiment, we replaced V440 with tryptophan and used the V440W mutant to compute a reference map. In this case, no additional density is visible in the scaled map despite W440 density being present in the reference map.
evidence: Shown in Figure 3C-D with V440W mutant reference

claim: Side chain densities are readily interpretable in the scaled map using a poly-alanine reference model despite the absence of any side chain information in the reference.
source: Finally, we truncated all side chains in the model and produced a poly-alanine model as a scaling reference. This procedure will substantially decrease the overall scattering mass of the reference. While side chain densities are slightly attenuated when compared at equivalent density threshold, they are readily interpretable despite the absence of any side chain information in the reference model.
evidence: Shown in Figure 3C-D with poly-alanine reference

claim: Side chain densities are readily observed for coordinate perturbations ranging from 2.5 to 50 Å r.m.s.d. despite the reference having no resemblance to the original structure.
source: In order to further assess the potential of coordinate bias, we randomly perturbed atom positions of the model within a mask encompassing the molecular outline and computed reference maps from the perturbed models to scale the experimental density. For perturbations ranging from 2.5 to 50 Å r.m.s.d., side chain densities are readily observed despite the reference having no resemblance to the original structure.
evidence: Shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A with perturbed coordinates

claim: A noticeable decrease in map contrast is observed with increasing coordinate r.m.s.d. perturbation.
source: We do, however, observe a noticeable decrease in map contrast with increasing r.m.s.d (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A

claim: Observed density features are the result of enhanced contrast and not of coordinate bias from the reference model.
source: Together, these results of mutating individual side chains and strongly perturbing model coordinates confirm that observed density features indeed are the result of enhanced contrast and not of coordinate bias from the reference model.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from mutant and perturbation experiments

claim: LocScale sharpening requires good estimates of atomic B-factors associated with the reference coordinates for best performance.
source: For best performance, LocScale sharpening requires good estimates of atomic B-factors associated with the reference coordinates.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from B-factor experiments

claim: Local scaling is sufficiently robust to result in improved maps even with reference structures for which atomic B-factors have not yet been refined.
source: We show, however, that local scaling is sufficiently robust to result in improved maps even with reference structures for which atomic B-factors have not yet been refined (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2

claim: Atomic B-factors correlate with local resolution when refinement proceeds robustly.
source: If refinement proceeds robustly, atomic B-factors are expected to correlate with local resolution estimates, as exemplified for Pol III (EMD-3180 and PDB ID 5fja; Figure 3—figure supplement 1G,H).
evidence: Shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1G,H for Pol III

claim: Underestimated atomic B-factors for peripheral subunits lead to density fragmentation in the scaled map.
source: Where atomic B-factors were underestimated (B ≤ 50 Å2) for model subunits located in the low-resolution map region at the particle periphery, the shallow falloff in the scaling reference led to density fragmentation in the scaled map (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B–D).
evidence: Shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2B-D

claim: Overestimated atomic B-factors within the core of the molecule result in blurring of well resolved secondary structure elements.
source: Conversely, a local amplitude profile that falls off too steeply by overestimated atomic B-factors within the core of the molecule (B ≥ 200 Å2) resulted in blurring of well resolved secondary structure elements in the respective scaled map (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B,C).
evidence: Shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2B,C

claim: Incorrectly estimated atomic B-factors can lead to a suboptimal representation of density features.
source: Therefore, in line with our results from reference window randomization, incorrectly estimated atomic B-factors can lead to a suboptimal representation of density features.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from B-factor experiments

claim: For correctly estimated atomic B-factor distributions, the level of blurring and sharpening is locally adapted for each region leading to optimized density contrast in the LocScale map.
source: For correctly estimated atomic B-factor distributions, the level of blurring and sharpening is locally adapted for each region leading to optimized density contrast in the LocScale map (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A–D).
evidence: Shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A-D

claim: Window sizes ranging from 25 to 35 Å appear to represent the expected features best.
source: Visual inspection of the resulting densities reveals overall similar appearance (Figure 3—figure supplement 3B; data shown representatively for V430-F449 helix), but window sizes ranging from 25 to 35 Å (20–30 pixels) appear to represent the expected features best.
evidence: Shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3B

claim: Map kurtosis peaks for window sizes between 20–35 Å, corresponding to the range for which Debye effects are strongest.
source: Kurtosis first increased, then decreased with increasing window size, peaking between 22–30 Å (Figure 3—figure supplement 3C). Maximal map kurtosis thus correlates with strongest deviation in the 7 to 4 Å region of the Guinier plot.
evidence: Shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3C

claim: An optimal window size can be chosen that best reflects the effective distance of local B-factor correlations, thus maximizing map kurtosis and Debye effect contrast.
source: Our results indicate that an optimal window size can be chosen that best reflects the effective distance of local B-factor correlations, thus maximizing map kurtosis and Debye effect contrast across the sharpened map.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from window size experiments

claim: The LocScale density contains enhanced local contrast and can be used as an improved target map for additional rounds of model building and refinement.
source: In a second step, we use the refined coordinate model to generate a reference map used for local amplitude scaling of the cryo-EM density. The LocScale density contains enhanced local contrast and can be used as an improved target map for additional rounds of model building and refinement.
evidence: Described in the workflow shown in Figure 4A

claim: The procedure can be iterated until convergence.
source: The procedure can be iterated until convergence (Figure 4A).
evidence: Described in the workflow shown in Figure 4A

claim: The iterative character of integrating the local scaling procedure into building and refinement workflows can be used to assist in extending an existing model to regions where no reference model was available at first.
source: One of the potential shortcomings of the proposed method is the principal requirement of an atomic model. The iterative character of integrating the local scaling procedure into building and refinement workflows, however, can be used to assist in extending an existing model to regions of the map where no reference model was available at first.
evidence: Demonstrated with TRPV1 model extension shown in Figure 4B

claim: The resulting LocScale density extended at least half the window size beyond the model until the density progressively disappeared.
source: As a density window of 25 Å was used for local scaling, the resulting LocScale density extended at least half the window size beyond the model until the density progressively disappeared.
evidence: Shown in Figure 4B with TRPV1 model extension

claim: The level of sharpening for adjacent density was approximately correct even in the absence of the complete model, and allowed the extension of the model.
source: In this case, the level of sharpening for an adjacent density was approximately correct even in the absence of the complete model, and allowed the extension of the model.
evidence: Shown in Figure 4B with TRPV1 model extension

claim: The LocScale map appears less noisy when compared with the deposited β-galactosidase map.
source: Qualitatively, the LocScale map appears less noisy when compared with the deposited map, which is supported by the smooth falloff of the radially averaged power spectrum profile (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Shown in Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A

claim: Density in the V728–H735 region of β-galactosidase is fragmented in the deposited map and precludes confident modelling of the backbone conformation.
source: Closer inspection of the deposited model and map revealed that density in this region is fragmented and precludes confident modelling of the backbone conformation (Figure 5D).
evidence: Shown in Figure 5D

claim: The LocScale density for V728–H735 showed a clear backbone trace and reveals that the deposited coordinates in this region are incompatible with the density.
source: By contrast, the LocScale density showed a clear backbone trace and reveals that the deposited coordinates in this region are incompatible with the density (Figure 5E).
evidence: Shown in Figure 5E

claim: The LocScale map allowed rebuilding of the V728–H735 residue stretch to better satisfy the density.
source: The LocScale map allowed us to rebuild this residue stretch to better satisfy the density (Figure 5F, Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Shown in Figure 5F and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B

claim: The V728–H735 conformation built and refined using the LocScale map is in closer agreement with the high-resolution crystal structure than the deposited model.
source: To verify our rebuilt conformation, we compared both PDB ID 5a1a and the rebuilt model with the 1.6 Å resolution crystal structure of E.coli β-galactosidase ([Wheatley et al., 2015], PDB ID 4ttg). The V728–H735 conformation built and refined using the LocScale map is in closer agreement with the high-resolution crystal structure than the deposited model (Figure 5–figure supplement 1D,E) and converges after two LocScale iterations alternating with model refinement (Figure 5—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: Shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1D,E,F

claim: The LocScale map for γ-secretase revealed additional density contrast at 9 out of 11 N-glycosylation sites.
source: Interestingly, when inspecting the γ-secretase LocScale map, we found additional density contrast at 9 out of 11 N-glycosylation sites, which would permit modeling glycan extensions beyond the deposited carbohydrate chains (Figure 5G–I).
evidence: Shown in Figure 5G-I

claim: The LocScale map revealed interpretable density at four additional and previously unreported N-linked glycosylation sites in γ-secretase.
source: Notably, in addition to previously described sites, the LocScale map revealed interpretable density at four additional and previously unreported N-linked glycosylation sites that allowed building of the glycan base (Figure 5J/K).
evidence: Shown in Figure 5J/K

claim: All parts of the LocScale map can be simultaneously visualized at a single threshold level.
source: One notable benefit of using locally scaled maps is that all parts of the map can be simultaneously visualized at a single threshold level.
evidence: Demonstrated with ribosome EF-Tu complex in Figure 6

claim: LocScale maps allow visualization of amino acid and nucleotide densities at a single threshold simultaneously.
source: LocScale maps allow visualization of amino acid and nucleotide densities at a single threshold simultaneously (Figure 6G,H).
evidence: Shown in Figure 6G,H for ribosome EF-Tu complex

claim: The most significant differences between overall and locally sharpened maps are observed in maps displaying large resolution variations.
source: The most significant differences between overall and locally sharpened maps are observed in maps displaying large resolution variations, such as RNA Pol III (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1

claim: LocScale maps provided enhanced contrast in regions of previously fragmented and weak density for TRPV1 and Pol III.
source: For both TRPV1 and Pol III, the respective LocScale maps provided enhanced contrast in regions of previously fragmented and weak density.
evidence: Demonstrated in Figure 7

claim: The LocScale maps allowed the rebuilding of loop regions and side chains in the TRPV1 structure.
source: The LocScale maps allowed the rebuilding of loop regions and side chains in the TRPV1 structure (Figure 7A–C) and confident placement of predicted secondary structure elements in previously less interpretable parts in the C82 subunit of Pol III (Figure 7D–F).
evidence: Shown in Figure 7A-C

claim: The LocScale maps allowed confident placement of predicted secondary structure elements in previously less interpretable parts in the C82 subunit of Pol III.
source: The LocScale maps allowed the rebuilding of loop regions and side chains in the TRPV1 structure (Figure 7A–C) and confident placement of predicted secondary structure elements in previously less interpretable parts in the C82 subunit of Pol III (Figure 7D–F).
evidence: Shown in Figure 7D-F

claim: The overall real-space correlation improved by 3–6% for models refined against the LocScale map when measured against the deposited EMDB entry.
source: In every case, the overall real-space correlation improved by 3–6% for models refined against the LocScale map when measured against the deposited EMDB entry (Table 1), and FSC curves computed between model maps and the original reconstructions show small but notable improvements of the LocScale model fit (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Shown in Table 1 and Figure 7—figure supplement 1

claim: FSC improvements are largest for TRPV1 and Pol III, for which the resolution differences across the map are largest.
source: It should be noted that comparisons of real-space correlation and model-map FSC measures are only meaningful when they are calculated against a common reference volume that has not undergone model-based scaling. FSC improvements are largest for TRPV1 and Pol III, for which also the resolution differences across the map are largest.
evidence: Inferred from Table 1 and Figure 7—figure supplement 1

claim: Improved EMRinger and Molprobity scores were found for all models refined with LocScale maps.
source: In addition, we find improved EMRinger and Molprobity scores (Barad et al., 2015; Chen et al., 2010) for all models refined with LocScale maps, indicating that better density fit is not achieved at the expense of model distortions.
evidence: Shown in Table 1

claim: Better density fit is not achieved at the expense of model distortions.
source: In addition, we find improved EMRinger and Molprobity scores (Barad et al., 2015; Chen et al., 2010) for all models refined with LocScale maps, indicating that better density fit is not achieved at the expense of model distortions.
evidence: Inferred from improved validation scores in Table 1

claim: LocRes maps partially compensate for artifacts arising from uniform sharpening in 3D reconstructions with significant resolution variation.
source: We observed that LocRes maps partially compensate for artifacts arising from uniform sharpening in 3D reconstructions with significant resolution variation, whereas local contrast optimization in LocScale maps consistently provides additional detail (Figure 7—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2

claim: Local contrast optimization in LocScale maps consistently provides additional detail compared to LocRes maps.
source: We observed that LocRes maps partially compensate for artifacts arising from uniform sharpening in 3D reconstructions with significant resolution variation, whereas local contrast optimization in LocScale maps consistently provides additional detail (Figure 7—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2

claim: Local contrast optimization by LocScale sharpening results in atomic models with improved overall density fit and good stereochemistry.
source: Together, the results from four examples show that local contrast optimization by LocScale sharpening results in atomic models with improved overall density fit and good stereochemistry.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from refinement statistics in Tables 1 and 2

claim: The LocScale method uses prior information from an atomic reference model that itself improves progressively during rounds of alternating coordinate refinement and LocScale sharpening.
source: We have introduced a procedure to improve the interpretability of cryo-EM density maps by model-based local sharpening. The LocScale method uses prior information from an atomic reference model that itself improves progressively during rounds of alternating coordinate refinement and LocScale sharpening.
evidence: Summary of the LocScale method

claim: The LocScale method is generally applicable to any cryo-EM structure whose density can be interpreted in terms of an atomic model.
source: Our method is generally applicable to any cryo-EM structure whose density can be interpreted in terms of an atomic model and thus only requires the input of density map and superimposed atomic coordinates without further specification of tuning parameters.
evidence: Description of method applicability

claim: Current contrast enhancing approaches often inadvertently result in either omission of structural detail or amplification of background noise.
source: Current contrast enhancing approaches often inadvertently result in either omission of structural detail or amplification of background noise, resulting in map artifacts that often cannot be easily distinguished from real atomic features.
evidence: Based on observations from comparing different sharpening methods

claim: LocScale maps represent high-resolution signal more accurately throughout the map by applying amplitude scaling locally.
source: By applying amplitude scaling locally, LocScale maps represent high-resolution signal more accurately throughout the map (Figures 2–7).
evidence: Demonstrated in Figures 2-7

claim: The LocScale procedure is reminiscent of an optimized low-pass filter that adaptively scales and filters the map amplitudes to match the local resolution and expected mass density distribution.
source: The procedure is reminiscent of an optimized low-pass filter that adaptively scales and filters the map amplitudes to match the local resolution and expected mass density distribution of the underlying molecular structure.
evidence: Description of the LocScale mechanism

claim: Reference-based scaling resulted in improved detail compared with local Guinier scaling.
source: While this approach, along with UNSHARP masking, remains a viable alternative for cases where no model is available, or is largely incomplete, we find that reference-based scaling resulted in improved detail compared with local Guinier scaling.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from comparison of sharpening methods

claim: Exponential sharpening is based on an approximation that assumes scattering to arise from randomly distributed free atoms.
source: Strictly speaking, exponential sharpening is based on an approximation that assumes scattering to arise from randomly distributed free atoms (Wilson, 1942).
evidence: Supported by citation to Wilson 1942

claim: LocScale amplitude scaling explicitly accounts for the characteristic local profile of the amplitude falloff due to specific structural properties of secondary structure motifs.
source: One advantage of LocScale amplitude scaling over other sharpening methods is that it explicitly accounts for the characteristic local profile of the amplitude falloff that is due to specific structural properties of secondary structure motifs (Morris et al., 2004) and can differ markedly from a simple exponential decay (Figure 2F, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by citation and shown in Figure 2F and Figure 2—figure supplement 1

claim: The magnitude of Debye effects positively correlates with kurtosis.
source: We find that the magnitude of these Debye effects positively correlates with kurtosis, where the latter represents a quantification of the apparent 'sharpness' of the density.
evidence: Inferred from analysis of Debye effects and kurtosis

claim: Map kurtosis represents a map quality indicator for cryo-EM densities similar to X-ray crystallographic maps.
source: Confirmed by visual inspection, we found that map kurtosis represents a map quality indicator for cryo-EM densities similar as proposed previously for X-ray crystallographic maps (Afonine et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to Afonine et al. 2015 and visual inspection

claim: Iterative LocScale contrast restoration consistently facilitates interpretability of density maps and accuracy of atomic models over a range of resolutions between 2 and 8 Å.
source: Using six examples, we showed that iterative LocScale contrast restoration consistently facilitates interpretability of density maps and accuracy of atomic models over a range of resolutions between 2 and 8 Å.
evidence: Demonstrated with six test cases

claim: LocScale maps facilitate visualization of detail in nucleic acid structures.
source: Notably, we also find LocScale maps to facilitate visualization of detail in nucleic acid structures.
evidence: Demonstrated with ribosome EF-Tu complex

claim: Reference scaling results in a map in which phosphate backbone and nucleotides can be visualized simultaneously with comparable detail at equivalent thresholds.
source: The effect can be partially compensated using reference scaling. The result is a map in which phosphate backbone and nucleotides can be visualized simultaneously with comparable detail at equivalent thresholds, thus facilitating model building.
evidence: Demonstrated with ribosome EF-Tu complex in Figure 6

claim: LocScale presents a form of model-based density improvement that is distinct from crystallographic density modification.
source: Although LocScale presents a form of model-based density improvement, it is important to distinguish our procedure from what is commonly understood by density modification in X-ray crystallographic refinement.
evidence: Explanation of the distinction between LocScale and crystallographic density modification

claim: In the LocScale approach, the amplitude component of density is modified to conform to prior expectations from a reference model, whereas the phase component remains unchanged.
source: In the LocScale approach put forward here, the amplitude component of density is modified such that it conforms to prior expectations from a reference model, whereas the phase component is retrieved directly from the experiment and remains unchanged by the procedure.
evidence: Description of the LocScale mechanism

claim: Reference coordinate bias from the atomic model is not present because the method is restricted to scaling of amplitudes against a radial average.
source: As the method is restricted to scaling of amplitudes against a radial average, we argue that reference coordinate bias from the atomic model is not present.
evidence: Argument based on the method design and supported by mutant experiments

claim: For cases with incomplete models or moderate conformational or register errors, the information stored in the radial amplitude profile provides a good initial estimate of the mass density distribution.
source: We show that for cases with incomplete models or moderate conformational or register errors in the model, the information stored in the radial amplitude profile still provides a good initial estimate of the mass density distribution and is sufficient to restore low contrast map features more clearly when compared with overall sharpening procedures (Figure 3E–F, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–E).
evidence: Shown in Figure 3E-F and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A-E

claim: Uniformly sharpened or globally scaled maps, optionally combined with filtering based on local resolution estimates, are appropriate starting targets for initial model building and refinement.
source: We find that either uniformly sharpened or globally scaled maps, optionally combined with filtering based on local resolution estimates, are appropriate starting targets for initial model building and refinement of atomic coordinates and B-factors.
evidence: Recommendation based on the workflow and results

claim: Once estimates of atomic B-factors have been obtained, LocScale maps provide locally optimized contrast and facilitate further rounds of model building and refinement.
source: Once estimates of atomic B-factors have been obtained, LocScale maps provide locally optimized contrast and facilitate further rounds of model building and refinement.
evidence: Recommendation based on the workflow and results

claim: Benefits of sharpening are confirmed for the LocScale maps, likely because locally optimized sharpening levels result in improvements of density fit and geometry over all map areas.
source: While it has been shown that map sharpening positively affects model refinement (Afonine et al., 2015; Joseph et al., 2016), a recent report suggested that overall benefits are limited (R. Y.-R. Wang et al., 2016). In our test cases with different ranges of resolution, we do confirm previously described benefits of sharpening also for the LocScale maps, likely because locally optimized sharpening levels result in improvements of density fit and geometry over all map areas.
evidence: Supported by citations and refinement statistics

claim: Cryo-EM maps degrade in quality towards the particle periphery due to limitations of current alignment and 3D reconstruction algorithms.
source: Regardless of resolution, cryo-EM maps degrade in quality towards the particle periphery due to limitations of current alignment and 3D reconstruction algorithms.
evidence: Based on known limitations of cryo-EM reconstruction methods

claim: True structural flexibility is expected to be more prominent in the particle periphery as vitrification captures the solution-state conformational landscape.
source: Furthermore, true structural flexibility is expected to be more prominent in the particle periphery as vitrification captures the solution-state conformational landscape at the respective experimental condition.
evidence: Based on understanding of molecular flexibility and cryo-EM sample preparation

claim: The LocScale procedure takes the concept of local filtering further by optimizing contrast through local amplitude scaling against an atomic reference model.
source: The need for approaches that address resolution variation has been recognized and local resolution filtering has been proposed (Cardone et al., 2013; Fernandez-Leiro and Scheres, 2017; Moriya et al., 2017). The LocScale procedure takes the concept of local filtering further by optimizing contrast of the cryo-EM density through local amplitude scaling against an atomic reference model.
evidence: Supported by citations and description of LocScale advantages

claim: Contrast improvements were particularly apparent in regions of increased structural flexibility such as peripheral subunits or flexible loop regions.
source: In the six presented test cases, contrast improvements were particularly apparent in regions of increased structural flexibility such as peripheral subunits or flexible loop regions, as well as partial occupancy sites of ligands, active site residues and carbohydrate chains at N-linked glycosylation sites.
evidence: Observed across six test cases

claim: Atomic model refinement followed by a local amplitude scaling step results in a single map that displays structural information optimally for all map areas simultaneously.
source: Atomic model refinement followed by a local amplitude scaling step results in a single map that displays structural information optimally for all map areas simultaneously, including those parts with large resolution variation.
evidence: Summary of LocScale benefits

claim: The LocScale procedure requires a large number of parameters and poses a risk of overfitting.
source: Due to the high number of voxels present in a 3D EM density map, our procedure requires a large number of parameters and poses a risk of overfitting.
evidence: Acknowledgment of potential limitation

claim: The LocScale implementation has two built-in safety features that prevent free fitting of parameters for every voxel.
source: Our implementation has two built-in safety features that prevent free fitting of the two parameters for every voxel.
evidence: Description of safeguards against overfitting

claim: The radial amplitude profile of the reference is estimated from a restrained model refinement procedure that can be assessed for overfitting.
source: First, the radial amplitude profile of the reference is estimated from a restrained model refinement procedure that can be assessed for overfitting.
evidence: Description of first safeguard against overfitting

claim: The chosen window size ensures that radial averaging over extended density regions leads to implicit correlations between scale factors over a certain distance.
source: Second, the chosen window size ensures that radial averaging over extended density regions, leading to implicit correlations between scale factors over a certain distance.
evidence: Description of second safeguard against overfitting

claim: The two fitted parameters are kept locally restrained, thus reducing the risk for overfitting of local sharpening profiles.
source: Consequently, the two fitted parameters are kept locally restrained, thus reducing the risk for overfitting of local sharpening profiles.
evidence: Conclusion about overfitting safeguards

claim: The agreement of B-factor and local resolution estimated on a per-residue basis can be used as a low-level assessment tool for the robustness of atomic B-factor refinement.
source: Considering that atomic B-factors represent the square amplitude of displacement from the refined coordinates they correlate with resolution. We thus propose to use the agreement of B-factor and local resolution estimated on a per-residue basis as a low-level assessment tool for the robustness of the atomic B-factor refinement (Figure 3—figure supplement 1G,H).
evidence: Shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1G,H

claim: Atomic B-factor refinement works acceptably up to a resolution of ~8 Å in the test cases investigated.
source: In the test cases investigated here, we found atomic B-factor refinement to work acceptably up to a resolution of ~8 Å.
evidence: Based on analysis of test cases

claim: The LocScale sharpening is expected to work best for near-atomic resolution cryo-EM reconstructions that allow reliable coordinate refinement including B-factors.
source: Therefore, we expect the LocScale sharpening to work best for near-atomic resolution cryo-EM reconstructions that are appropriate for model building and allow reliable coordinate refinement including B-factors.
evidence: Conclusion about optimal application range

claim: Inspection of FSCref curves often displays notable disagreement between FSCref and half-map FSCs at low resolution despite good real-space density correlations.
source: Interestingly, inspection of FSCref curves often displays notable disagreement between FSCref and half-map FSCs at low resolution despite good real-space density correlations between the model and density map, indicating that additional efforts are required to accurately model molecular structure factors including solvent contributions (Clarage et al., 1992; Jiang and Brunger, 1994); and the need for inclusion of more sophisticated B-factor models to reflect concerted molecular motion of atom groups in cryo-EM model refinement strategies (Painter and Merritt, 2006).
evidence: Observed in FSCref analysis and supported by citations

claim: Atomic models will become more tightly integrated into the cryo-EM structure determination process in the future.
source: For the future of cryo-EM, it is tempting to speculate that atomic models will become more tightly integrated into the structure determination process.
evidence: Speculation about future developments

claim: Up-stream parts of the structure determination process such as orientation search may benefit from efforts that aim at iteratively improving both density map and atomic model.
source: In principle, up-stream parts of the structure determination process such as the orientation search of the particle images for 3D reconstruction may also benefit from efforts that aim at iteratively improving both density map and atomic model, analogous to X-ray crystallography procedures that refine the atomic model against diffraction data.
evidence: Speculation about potential future applications

claim: The LocScale procedure results in more faithful density representations and overcomes previous shortcomings in dealing with maps displaying considerable resolution variation.
source: We here put forward an alternative procedure for iterative cryo-EM density sharpening that makes use of local amplitude scaling derived from a refined atomic reference model. In our examples, the LocScale procedure results in more faithful density representations and at the same time overcomes previous shortcomings in dealing with maps displaying considerable resolution variation.
evidence: Summary conclusion from all results

claim: The LocScale approach is expected to benefit a wide range of cryo-EM structures and will facilitate atomic model interpretation of the rapidly growing number of high-resolution cryo-EM density maps.
source: The approach is expected to benefit a wide range of cryo-EM structures and will facilitate atomic model interpretation of the rapidly growing number of high-resolution cryo-EM density maps.
evidence: Conclusion about expected impact
